newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says Bre-X needs fresh Busang approval.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says Bre-X needs fresh Busang approval.

text.p: Indonesia said on Thursday Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp must jointly submit applications for contracts of work to develop the huge Busang gold find in East Kalimantan.

Mines and Energy Ministry secretary-general Umar Said said the applications must be presented by a joint venture the two firms must set-up if they want to develop the find, estimated by Bre-X to contain at least 57 million ounces of gold.
"Now that they have agreed to be partners in developing Busang, they must set up a joint venture company and make a fresh application for contracts of work," he told Reuters.
But a source close to the talks between Bre-X and Barrick said they two companies had not yet struck a partnership deal.
"We have not reached an agreement," the source, speaking on condition of anonymity, told Reuters in Jakarta. "There are still outstanding points, and that's where we are."
The Indonesian government, in a letter last month, told the companies to enter a partnership agreement, with Bre-X retaining a 25 percent stake in the find and Barrick 75 percent.
It also wanted the two companies to allocate the Indonesian government a 10 percent stake in the property.

Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana told reporters late on Wednesday that the government had cancelled parliamentary approval of applications for contracts of work made by Bre-X to develop the richest parts of Busang.
"We cancel it. The Bre-X contract of work will be processed from the beginning," Sudjana told reporters after a marathon parliamentary commission hearing.
Sudjana's statement led to Bre-X requesting a suspension of its stock on the Toronto Stock Exchange.

Umar said on Thursday that the joint application would go through the normal process of getting approvals from the director-general of mining, the Mines and Energy Minister, parliament and finally President Suharto.
"The government has stopped processing the previous application for contracts of work by Bre-X because of various problems," he said.
"Therefore, the previous application by Bre-X that has been delayed must be stopped and must be said to have been cancelled," he said.
The source said Bre-X and Barrick would only jointly submit a fresh application for contracts of work when they complete the partnership deal as proposed by the Indonesian government.
"When Bre-X and Barrick come to an agreement, they will form a joint venture company which will make a fresh application for the contracts of work," the source said.
"This could take a long time," he said.

The source said Bre-X had yet to receive a reply from the Mines and Energy Ministry on its request for more time to seek shareholders' approval on the government's proposed 25-75 percent split in the Busang property between Bre-X and Barrick.

Meanwhile, Indonesian businessman Jusuf Merukh, who claims to own 40 percent of the Busang find, said on Thursday he would seek a clarification from Sudjana on the cancellation of parliamentary approval of the Bre-X contracts.
"I will send a letter to the minister seeking a clarification tomorrow (Friday)," he told Reuters.
